text.tspan: The pattern on the left mirrors the shape on the right. Three dots collect on the left, and expand on the right.
const user = { id: 7, name: 'Ada', city: 'Bath', tz: 'GMT' };
const { name, city: town, role = 'guest', ...rest } = user;
role = 'guest' → default, the key was missing
rest = { id: 7, tz: 'GMT' } → everything left over
REST: on the left of the equals
Gathers what is left into one new value.
SPREAD: on the right, or in a call
Spreading copies only ONE level deep: a nested object is still shared with the original. Later keys win, which is how
{ ...defaults, ...options } works. And destructuring a function parameter, function f({ id, name }), gives named arguments.
